newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro sees steady oil output in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro sees steady oil output in 1997.

text.p: Norsk Hydro ASA said on Monday it expected equity oil and gas production to remain on the same level as in 1996 at around 13.5 million tonnes of oil equivalent.
The company said its production profile was generally increasing over the medium term.

But due to an asset exchange agreement, Hydro's share of the North Sea Veslefrikk and part of its equity in the Njord development in the Norwegian Sea, and associated future production, were transferred to Petro-Canada.
"Production in 1997 is therefore expected to be on about the same level as in 1996," Hydro said in a statement announcing 1996 results.
The company added that there was uncertainty over the future direction of oil prices due to increasing OPEC and non-OPEC output, along with the resumption of Iraqi crude exports.
